html:
French Somaliland was a small French colony on the Gulf of Aden in the Horn of Africa, from the 1880s to 1967. It is now Djibouti.

France bought the anchorage of Obock in 1862 and signed treaties with local Afar and Somali rulers in the 1880s. It wanted a coaling station of its own on the route through the Suez Canal to Madagascar and Indochina. The new town of Djibouti became the capital in 1896.

Its value came from its neighbour. A French built railway from Djibouti to Addis Ababa, finished in 1917, carried most of the trade of the Ethiopian Empire. The colony sat between British Somaliland and Italian Eritrea.

During World War II it stayed loyal to Vichy France until late 1942. Voters chose to stay French in 1958 and again in 1967, the second time amid protests and claims of fraud. That year it was renamed the French Territory of the Afars and the Issas.
sum: French Somaliland was a small French colony on the Gulf of Aden in the Horn of Africa, from the 1880s to 1967. It is now Djibouti.
